research.title: What Is the Outlook for Diesel and Gasoline Supplies?
research.summary: Energy markets have been surprisingly resilient amid the disruption to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. However, there are few signs of relief in markets for refined products such as diesel, gasoline, and jet fuel, says Nitin Jindal, head of Global Commodities in Goldman Sachs FICC and Equities, on The Markets podcast. Jindal also discusses China’s remarkable adjustment to the disruption in energy supplies and the outlook for natural gas prices in Europe as winter approaches.

research.title: Jackson Hole Tests the Fed’s Framework
research.summary: Investors are keeping a close eye on Jackson Hole for signals on the economic outlook and the path for rates. Our Chief U.S. economist Michael Gapen joins Global Head of Macro Strategy Matthew Hornbach to discuss whether markets get what they want—or what the Fed needs. Read more insights from Morgan Stanley.

research.title: The capital required for critical supply chains
research.summary: In this episode of J.P. Morgan’s Making Sense, Michael Johnson, Security and Resiliency Initiative lead for Energy and the U.S. Government, sits down with Ben Wilson, Co-head of North American Mergers & Acquisitions, and Andrew Castaldo, Co-head of Mid-Cap Mergers & Acquisitions, to weigh in on the future of global supply chains. Over the course of the conversation, they cover critical mineral supply chains, manufacturing bottlenecks, and the shift from just-in-time to just-in-case inventory.

research.title: Volatility is no longer the exception
research.summary: Geopolitical shocks, commodity swings, retail flows, and rapid reversals are changing how markets move. Explore how institutional traders are managing volatility as an ongoing condition—using data, technology, and judgment to respond faster and think further ahead.

research.title: U.S. Earnings Are Exceptional. Stocks Are Playing Catch-Up
research.summary: Corporate profits are on a tear, but stocks haven’t fully reflected them. We unpack the forces capping valuations: yields, oil and the artificial intelligence cycle’s proof point.
